rationale.conceptual: The method relies on well-known protocols (DFT geometry relaxation, HSE06 hybrid functional band structure, OER free-energy calculation with CHE) but demands careful implementation of band alignment extraction from layer-projected states, classification of Z-scheme/Type-II, and vibrational/entropy corrections. It is a multi-part documented algorithm, not a textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves constructing a heterostructure, applying five strain conditions, running geometry relaxations (PBE+vdW), performing HSE06 band calculations, adsorbing OER intermediates with vibrational analysis, and computing thermodynamic quantities, all orchestrated with an open-source DFT code. The multi-stage workflow and environment setup (HSE06 support, pseudopotentials) make the orchestration demanding.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper uses standard first-principles DFT (PBE+vdW, HSE06) and the computational hydrogen electrode model to compute band structures and OER free energies of a 2D heterostructure under strain. The reproduction task requires implementing a multi-stage DFT pipeline with hybrid functional and vibrational corrections, which is non-trivial but established. The required compute resources are modest (small supercell, CPU-based).

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT with hybrid functional on a ~40-atom slab for five strain cases and a few adsorbates is CPU-bound; a multi-core workstation with ~8 GB RAM suffices. Input structures are tiny (kB scale), so data volume is negligible.
